result.question: Discuss the reforms through which Meiji Japan built a modern nation-state. (Answer in 150 words)

directives.meaning: Look at the issue from more than one side, with reasons, and reach a balanced view.

sentences.text: The arrival of the American Commodore Perry in 1853 to demand trade unsettled Tokugawa rule, and in 1868 the Meiji Restoration removed the shogun and restored the emperor.
Japan was not wholly isolated before this, having access to wider knowledge through the Dutch and the Chinese.
Under the slogan fukoku kyohei (rich country, strong army), the new leaders sought to avoid being colonised like India.
An emperor system made the emperor, revered as a descendant of the Sun Goddess, the symbol of the nation and of westernisation.
Schooling became compulsory for boys and girls, with stress on loyalty and Japanese history.
All young men over twenty had to do military service.
The economy was modernised through an agricultural tax, the Tokyo-Yokohama railway, modern banks and subsidies to firms like Mitsubishi.
The Meiji Constitution of 1889 created a Diet with limited powers.
Victories over China and Russia displayed Japan's new strength.
Japan's state-led modernisation offers lessons for developing nations, though its slide into militarism shows the cost of weak democratic checks.
